engagement_background.objective: Advantia Health engaged Treya Partners to quickly reduce procurement costs and strengthen purchasing discipline by executing strategic sourcing across key spend areas and establishing improved procurement processes that support private-equity value-creation goals.
engagement_background.scope_summary: Treya will pursue savings creation in up to 10 spend categories representing approximately $19M of addressable spend out of a $45M total AP/P-card universe. Categories include Employee Benefits (optional), Medical Devices & Equipment, Diagnostic/Lab services, Billing/RCM, Medical Supplies, Telecom, Data Center/Cloud Hosting, Electronic Payment Processing, and Office Supplies; some sub-categories may be excluded if deemed un-addressable after deep-dives.
constraints_challenges: Limited strategic procurement focus and resources prior to engagement
Spend and item-level data scattered across two separate AP/P-card systems with gaps in supplier usage details
Ongoing post-acquisition integration issues between Advantia (Mid-Atlantic) and Heartland business units
Potential resistance to changing long-standing clinical suppliers and need to avoid business disruption
Six-month project timeline (plus a later Benefits work-stream) imposes tight sequencing of sourcing waves
Requirement for Advantia to cease parallel purchasing activity in scoped categories to prevent market confusion

procurement_environment.data_availability: Header-level AP and P-card spend data from Advantia and Heartland systems were available; line-item usage data and contracts had to be requested from suppliers and were often incomplete.
procurement_environment.data_quality_notes: Multiple spend files with inconsistent vendor naming, limited item descriptions, no centralized contract repository, and non-responsive suppliers created visibility gaps.
